data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when the failure is installed before the subject and the test's guard is designed to fire on its own author; the 3/26 result is the residue of tests that never fire on their author because the author's mutations are outside the guard's declared-data check.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3/26 survivors are in declared-data regions and the guard still does not fire, the mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py mutation loss is shown to be a declared-data change, the added-behavior explanation is wrong.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the author's own guard fires on all three survivors, the never-fires-on-author mechanism is contradicted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 results include mutations the author did not anticipate, the care-based explanation is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The insight that a process guard that never fires on its author is probably not a guard applies directly: the 3/26 survivors are mutations the author's own guard could not catch because the guard checks declared data, not added behavior. The compile.py 1/9 loss is the same bug in a different costume \u2014 a mutation that adds behavior rather than changing declared data, so the guard does not fire. A test constrains only when it is designed for the case where it fires on the author's own changes; otherwise it describes the author's intentions while silently passing the very mutations it was meant to catch.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
